keyFindings.description: A term taken from a graceful hand-back (HandedBack) still sets stale_binding when the durable is push-bound, and it always is then: the stopping pod lingers on its subscription by design. Nothing clears it for the rest of the term (only a begin that finds the durable unbound, line 477), so the term's release carries stale_binding and the next holder computes handedBack false (lease.go:806) and settles with the 7 s ack-wait cap. From the second graceful hand-over on (a rolling deploy's second pod), a stop with a prompt in hand past the 3 s grace (cancelled, NAKed with a delay, so outstanding) delivers about 3 + 1 + 0.5 + 7 = 11.5 s after SIGTERM, past the 10 s graceful bound. The deep-review subagent's scratch probe: C took B's record with handedBack=false, cap 7s, held_ms 7000 with a 30 s retry outstanding. Every graceful row starts from mpStartPair's first record, so none covers it.

abandon (new in d19302d3) gives the lease up without clearing awaitedBinding, which only a successful begin clears. A pod that gave up while waiting out a binding later takes an expired record from a holder that died hard and computes settle false (line 442), as if the expiry were its own lapsed renewal: it skips the hold (the dead pod's messages after newer ones) or waits out a lost node's binding for minutes.
